The expert incorrectly assumes that because there are only a few valid distributions, Bob can simply guess the exact numbers for all of them simultaneously. However, Bob does not know which specific distribution (e.g., 6-12-12 vs 8-8-14) is the actual one; he only knows the constraints. He must submit three guesses that work for *any* possible valid distribution. The expert's calculation that he wins $30,000 (all 30 coins) is incorrect because it is impossible to guess the exact count for three unknown boxes while satisfying the condition that guesses must be $\le$ actual counts for all boxes in all scenarios. For instance, if the distribution is 6-12-12, guessing 8, 8, 14 would result in losing the first box (guess 8 > actual 6) and winning the others, totaling $22,000. The expert failed to perform the necessary minimax analysis to find the minimum guaranteed winnings across all possible distributions.
